title: The Breakthrough: Open the Outside File
summary: Give up the second pawn to pull a defender away and leave the outside pawn a clear path to promotion.

nodes.question: Should White recapture, or offer another pawn?
nodes.explanation: Begin after b6 ...axb6 in the physical demonstration. White has Kh1 and pawns a5/c5 against Kh3 and pawns b6/b7/c7. The earlier eight-piece b6 decision is source context.

branches.title: Sacrifice c6 to free the a-pawn
commentary: Begin after b6 ...axb6 in the physical demonstration. White has Kh1 and pawns a5/c5 against Kh3 and pawns b6/b7/c7. The earlier eight-piece b6 decision is source context.
c6 offers the second pawn. Its purpose is to pull b7 away from the seventh rank, leaving the a-file free.
bxc6 accepts the second sacrifice. This is the illustrated defensive capture.
a6 advances the surviving outside pawn on the cleared file.
c5 starts a counter-race with Black’s newly created passer.
a7 moves one square from promotion. Black’s pawn is still farther away.
c4 continues the counter-race but does not stop a8.
a8=Q promotes first. The exact queen-versus-pawns ending is winning for White; full queen conversion is outside this branch.
branches.explanation: a8=Q promotes first. The exact queen-versus-pawns ending is winning for White; full queen conversion is outside this branch.

branches.title: Independent automatic recaptures lose the race
commentary: Begin after b6 ...axb6 in the physical demonstration. White has Kh1 and pawns a5/c5 against Kh3 and pawns b6/b7/c7. The earlier eight-piece b6 decision is source context.
axb6 abandons the winning breakthrough. The exact resulting position is losing for White against best defense. Black is not obliged to make an automatic recapture.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: Automatic recapture abandons the winning breakthrough and loses against best defense.

branches.title: Independent refusal leaves the other passer
commentary: Begin after b6 ...axb6 in the physical demonstration. White has Kh1 and pawns a5/c5 against Kh3 and pawns b6/b7/c7. The earlier eight-piece b6 decision is source context.
c6 creates the breakthrough threat.
b5 declines the offer and advances the b6 pawn. This is an independently chosen alternative, not an assertion that the source illustrates it.
cxb7 removes the other b-pawn and leaves White one step from promotion.
b4 pursues the counter-race too slowly.
b8=Q promotes. The exact position remains winning for White, so declining the offered c6 pawn does not rescue this selected defense.
branches.classification: independent alternative with representative legal replies
branches.explanation: b8=Q promotes. The exact position remains winning for White, so declining the offered c6 pawn does not rescue this selected defense.

branches.title: Independent recaptures create a drawn pawn wall
commentary: Begin after b6 ...axb6 in the physical demonstration. White has Kh1 and pawns a5/c5 against Kh3 and pawns b6/b7/c7. The earlier eight-piece b6 decision is source context.
axb6 gives up the win and actually leaves Black a winning position with best play.
cxb6 automatically recaptures instead of preserving that advantage. This particular reply gives White a draw.
cxb6 leaves White b6 facing Black b7. Neither pawn can advance or capture the opposing pawn directly ahead, and the exact king-and-pawn ending is drawn.
branches.classification: independent comparison with a suboptimal Black recapture
branches.explanation: The selected automatic-recapture sequence draws, but Black could instead preserve a win after axb6.

exercises.prompt: Why offer a second pawn instead of recovering material?
exercises.answer: Capturing c6 pulls the b7 pawn away from the outside passer. White needs a clear promotion file more than a balanced pawn count.

startContext: Begin at the saved seven-piece position after b6 ...axb6 at 26s. The physical board is reviewed square by square; the kings remain on h1/h3. The initial eight-piece b6 choice is not claimed as exactly solved here. The c6/bxc6/a-pawn race is illustrated; automatic-recapture and declined-sacrifice comparisons use independent representative replies.
